passages.note: The engrossed text keeps map-drawing with the legislature, adds mid-decade amendment authority, enacts a new 2026 map and narrows judicial remedies, but a No vote does not say which of those parts he rejected.
Bill details page for the same instrument; it names the authors and sponsors (Bray is not among them) and records the defeat on third reading.

rows.reasoning: Bray voted Nay on HB 1032 (2026), a bill that would have let the general assembly amend congressional districts mid-decade, enacted a new map and restricted judicial remedies against apportionment. A No vote rules out the side of "the party that controls the state legislature without outside interference" but names no rung of its own: nothing in the record shows he wants "independent citizens' commissions with no elected officials involved at any level", a commission "with equal representation from both major parties", a "bipartisan legislative committee" with supermajority approval, or "state legislatures with court oversight". Excluding one rung is not evidence for any of the others (V4.2).
